description: Streaming anomaly detection in Python for multivariate and univariate data streams: 53 online detectors (LODA, HalfSpaceTrees, RRCF, RSHash, xStream, SeasonalHybridESD, DAMP, SAND), conformal & SPOT alert calibration, drift monitoring, composable pipelines, and prequential evaluation.
rules: Use fit_partial(x), score_partial(x), and fit_score_partial(x) on 1-D arrays of shape (num_features,); never use deprecated or nonexistent APIs like fit_predict or Evaluator.
Higher scores always mean more anomalous instances across every detector, postprocessor, ensembler, and calibrator.
score_partial(x) never mutates model state; use fit_score_partial(x) for prequential score-before-learn evaluation.
Univariate detectors expect a 1-D array of shape (1,), such as np.array([value]), not a scalar or shape (1, 1); reshape 1-D series with values.reshape(-1, 1) for ArrayStreamer.
Compose streaming pipelines with `|` (StreamPipeline, e.g. StandardScaler() | LODA() | ConformalProbabilityCalibrator()) and ensemble detectors with `&` (ModelEnsemble).

Convert arbitrary raw scores into [0, 1] alert scales using ConformalProbabilityCalibrator, SPOTProbabilityCalibrator, or GaussianTailProbabilityCalibrator, paired with ThresholdFilter or QuantileFilter.
Evaluate labeled streams prequentially with pysad.evaluation.evaluate_stream and streaming metrics such as AUROCMetric, AUPRMetric, PrecisionMetric, RecallMetric, RollingMetric, and WindowedMetric.
Import public classes from their subpackages (pysad.models, pysad.integrations, pysad.utils, pysad.evaluation, pysad.statistics, pysad.transform.*) rather than private module paths.
Use LODA.explain_partial(x), HalfSpaceTrees.explain_partial(x), or KitNet.explain_partial(x) to attribute per-feature contributions to an anomaly score.

Run PyOD batch models on streams with ReferenceWindowModel or OneFitModel, embed PySAD detectors in River or scikit-learn with RiverAnomalyDetector or SklearnAnomalyDetector, and score River forecasters with PredictiveAnomalyDetector.
